requirements.title: The character intrinsic operator concatenates same-kind character operands and produces character result type
requirements.definition: The character intrinsic operator // concatenates two operands of type character with the same kind type parameter, and evaluating the character intrinsic operation produces a result of type character.

pending.nondefault-same-kind-profile: PENDING profile-qualified source shape using a portable selected nondefault character kind only when available. Absence of such a kind makes the finite witness unavailable, not failed.
pending.different-kind-boundary: PENDING diagnostic/control source shape for // operands of different character kind type parameters, paired with a same-kind repair. The plan must independently establish both kinds and exclude literal-kind syntax errors.

requirements.oracle:
Character value oracles must compare equal-length character values or assert LEN explicitly before comparison; shorter-operand blank padding in relational comparisons cannot be used to hide a wrong concatenation length.

S10.1.5.3.1-001 default character concatenation runtime fixtures: two complete run/positive-control/f2023 programs use only default CHARACTER operands. The default-same-kind case checks KIND(left)==KIND(right), KIND(left//right)==KIND(left), LEN(left//right)==5 and the exact equal-length value 'AXb7q' from left 'AX' followed by right 'b7q'. The result-type case assigns left 'R4' // right 's9T' to a declared CHARACTER(LEN=5) variable, then checks the assigned equal-length value, LEN(result)==5 and KIND(result)==KIND(left). These are runtime type/kind/length witnesses, not storage-byte or TRANSFER tests.

requirements.title: Character concatenation forms the right-appended value with length equal to the sum of operand lengths
requirements.definition: Table 10.4 interprets x1 // x2 as concatenating x1 with x2. The result value is the value of x1 concatenated on the right with the value of x2, and the result length is the sum of the operand lengths. The table has a single row and its column extraction is unambiguous after row-by-row checking.
requirements.oracle:
Always assert LEN for concatenation results and use expected character values of the same length as the result. Do not credit comparisons where relational blank padding could make an incorrect length appear equal.

S10.1.5.3.1-002 character concatenation value runtime fixtures: four complete run/effect/f2023 programs observe Table 10.4 and p3. Distinct default-character operands of unequal lengths make swapped order and wrong length visible. The right-append case uses left 'AB' and right 'q7Z', expecting LEN 5 and equal-length value 'ABq7Z'; swapping would be 'q7ZAB'. The length-sum case uses left 'mN' and right 'p8R', expecting LEN 5 from 2+3 and value 'mNp8R'. The zero-length-left case uses LEN(left)==0 and right 'R9q', expecting LEN 3 and value 'R9q'. The zero-length-right case uses left 'L0xP' and LEN(right)==0, expecting LEN 4 and value 'L0xP'. Every value comparison is against an equal-length literal and every length facet has an explicit LEN guard.

requirements.title: Parentheses specifying evaluation order do not affect the value of a character expression
requirements.source: 10.1.5.3.1 p3 final sentence; J3/24-007 PDF p178.
requirements.definition: For character expressions using the character intrinsic operation, parentheses used to specify the order of evaluation have no effect on the character expression's value.
requirements.oracle:
Observe only the final character value and length. Parentheses here do not license any inference about whether a particular operand expression was evaluated before another.

S10.1.5.3.1-003 character parentheses runtime fixtures: three complete run/effect/f2023 programs observe only final value and length for parenthesized character concatenation. The left-grouped case evaluates ('A'//'bc')//'D3e' and expects LEN 6 and value 'AbcD3e'. The right-grouped case evaluates 'A'//('bc'//'D3e') with the same LEN 6 and value. The nested-parentheses case evaluates ((( 'u' )))//(('V2')//(('wx9'))) without relying on operand evaluation order, expecting LEN 6 and equal-length value 'uV2wx9'.

review_rationale: Renewal of the content-bound source review for 10.1.5.3.1 after a fixture packet bound facets into this catalogue. Adding a facet binding changes catalogue content and therefore stales the recorded source review by design; this renewal records that the staleness is attributable solely to the binding. The SOURCE ACCOUNTING IS UNCHANGED by the fixture packets: no base or fine unit was added, removed or redispositioned, no requirement was added or deleted, no requirement identifier was renumbered or reused, and the section's unit hashes against the pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...) are exactly those verified by the original independent source review recorded in the corresponding doc/source_audits receipt. What changed is that facets which were previously pending are now bound to executable fixtures, each of which was independently reviewed as a fixture in its own right, with non-vacuity established by mutation rather than inspection and with the frozen LFortran and the gfortran f2023 qualifying reference both reproduced by the integrator before any adjudication was recorded. This renewal therefore carries forward the original source review's findings unchanged and adds no new source claim. It is not fixture approval, which is recorded separately per case in tests/reviews.json, and it confers no additional execution or coverage credit beyond what those per-case adjudications already state. All facets not bound by a fixture packet remain pending exactly as the original source review left them.
